subject: Covid-19
description: Order Re Protective Face Coverings in Court Facilities
issuer: Multnomah County Circuit Court — Presiding Judge
title: Multnomah County Circuit Court Presiding Judge Order — 2101-00000 (5); Covid-19
text:
IN THE CIRCUIT COURT OF THE STATE OF OREGON
FOR MULTNOMAH COUNTY
In t he Matter of Implementing
Chief Justice Order No. 21-025
PRESIDING JUDGE ORDER NO. 2101-00000
ORDER RE PROTECTIVE FACE COVERINGS IN
COURT FACILITIES
On March 8, 2020, Oregon Governor Kate Brown issued Executive Order 20-03 decla ring a state
of emergency due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The state of emergency has been extended, but it is
scheduled to expire on June 28, 2021. On June 25, 2021, Governor Brown issued Executive Order 21-15,
which extended the state of emergency until December 31, 2021, but lifted the protective face covering
requirements, social distancing and other restrictions effective June 30, 2021.
On June 1, 2020, I issued Presiding Judge Order (PJO) 2001-00000, requiring all persons ent ering
court fac ilities in Multnomah County to wear protective face coverings. On October 28, 2020, Oregon
Chief Justice Martha Walte rs issued Chief Justice Order (CJO) 20-045, requiring protective face coverings
in all state court faci lities.
On June 28, 2021, Chief Justice Walters issued CJO 21-025, which lifted many restrict ions
previously imposed on court operations following the expiration of the state of emergency. CJO 21-025
lifts the protective face cove rings requirement previously imposed under CJO 20-045 and aut horizes
Presiding Judges in each judicial district to impose protective face covering requirements consistent with
county requirements or as needed to protect public health and safety.
On June 29, 2021, Multnomah County Chair Deborah Kafoury announced t hat protective face
coverings would continue to be required for staff working in county faci lities, and would be
recommended for members of the public entering county faci lit ies, until August 1, 2021,
notwit hstanding Governor Brown's action generally lifting the protective face covering requirement
statewide.
Accordingly, pursuant to the authority stated in CJO 21-025, consistent with Multnomah County
policy and to protect public health and safety, I hereby ORDER as fo llows:
1. Definitions. "Courthouse" means the common areas open to the public--including without
limitation hallways, elevators, the jury assembly room, public service counters, and other public
areas, and individual courtrooms-in the Mult nomah County Courthouse, the Juvenile Justice
Center, the Downtown Justice Center, and the East County Courthouse. "Protective face
1
covering" means a covering of the nose and mouth to protect against spreading the COVID-19
virus, as recommended by the Centers for Disease Control.
2. Except for witnesses while testifying, children under two (2) years of age, and as provided in
paragraphs 3 and 4 below, all persons entering the Courthouse are required to wear a
protective face covering while in the Courthouse.
3. A judge presiding over a trial or other proceeding in a courtroom may, in the judge's sole
discretion, allow any person participating in or attending the proceeding to remove the
protective face covering upon showing proof that the person has been fully vaccinated against
the COVID-19 virus. A judge may also al low jurors during voir dire to temporarily remove their
protective face covering to the extent the judge deems the removal appropriate for the jury
selection process. Judges and court staff who have been fully vaccinated are not required to
wear protective face coverings in the courtroom during a court proceeding.
4. Any person seeking to enter the Courthouse without using a protective face covering because of
disability, respiratory or other health-related issues, or otherwise for good cause can request an
exemption from the Presiding Judge. Exemption requests may be presented to the Presiding
Judge at the times set for ex parte matters or other times as needed. Persons requesting such
an exemption should contact Presiding Court before entering the Courthouse.
5. The Court will continue to provide protective face coverings and information about how to use
them as needed and as available resources allow.
6. This ORDER is effective on June 30, 2021, and will remain in effect until August 1, 2021, unless
extended by further order of this Court.
DATED: June 29, 2021
Stephen . Bushong
Presiding Judge, Multnomah County Circuit Court
